title: Retained supplier aliases cross a scalar catalog reader contract
fault_primitive: MongoDB multikey alias revisions shadow scalar hotel profiles while BSON address cardinality changes from object to array
incident_class: Partial supplier catalog schema migration against a legacy reader
symptoms: Search and recommendation responses trigger frontend nil-address serialization panics despite successful profile RPCs and healthy pods. Frontend runtime-error logs surge.
why_hard: Every current scalar profile remains intact. Retained revisions have complete addresses and no retirement markers, but use arrays for supplier aliases and address cardinality. MongoDB scalar equality matches their multikey IDs; the Go BSON reader silently drops incompatible array fields and caches an incomplete successful response indefinitely. Missing-address checks find zero rows and the parent's duplicate-ID aggregation finds zero duplicate groups because scalar and array keys group separately. Restoring scalar profiles, restarting services, flushing caches, deleting lifecycle-retired rows, and adding a unique ID index do not repair the persisted schema mismatch. Diagnosis requires correlating MongoDB equality and grouping semantics, BSON types, cached JSON, and the legacy protobuf model.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Remove records missing addresses or marked retired and find none
Inspect canonical scalar profiles and dismiss storage
Try a unique ID index without resolving multikey alias overlap
Flush cache or restart profile and repopulate incompatible revisions
Treat successful profile spans as proof of complete responses
mitigation_summary: Find array-valued identity revisions, verify that exactly one alias has an intact scalar canonical profile, remove only those incompatible revisions, then flush the profile cache. No saved state is required.
